newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: WOMAN REMAINS CRITICAL AFTER LIGHTNING STRIKE
A 42-year-old Coburg woman is in a critical condition at the Geelong Hospital this morning following yesterday's fatal lightning strike.
A couple was killed and several people were injured by the strike, during a church picnic.
About 20 members of Coburg's Arabic Baptist Church were picnicking in Geelong's Eastern Gardens, when lightning struck a rotunda they were sheltering under at around nine o'clock yesterday morning.
Relatives of the dead couple are looking after their 10 and 12 year old sons, and church followers are undergoing trauma counselling.
CONTROVERSIAL SHIP SETS SAIL
A bulk carrier which has been at the centre of a row over the alleged mistreatment and non-payent of wages to its crew has left the port of Newcastle bound for Chile.
The Greek owners of the MV Hunter put up a A$200,000 bond at the weekend, allowing the vessel to be released from admiralty arrest.
The ship left the port last night with a replacement crew.

Meanwhile, discussions will take place in Sydney today between the International Transport Workers' Federation and the ship's owners, in a bid to recover wages owed to 11 crew members still in Newcastle.
ECONOMIC UPSWING TIPPED FOR LATE '97
A five year business outlook compiled by a top economic forecaster is predicting a mixed outlook for the states and territories.
Access Economics is tipping an economic upswing by the end of this year, with Queensland and Western Australia surging ahead.
But the news isn't as good for Tasmania, the ACT and South Australia, where Access predicts continued subdued economic activity.

The outlook for New South Wales is mixed, despite an Olympics boost, and an economic slowdown is tipped for Victoria. Access Director, Chris Richardson, says the upswing predicted for late in the year should be sustained, with housing, jobs and retail sales all picking up.
Mr Richardson expects unemployment to peak at around nine percent in the middle of this year.
MINERALS COUNCIL WISHES JAWOYN SUCCESS
The Northern Territory Minerals Council says mining and exploration agreements involving Aboriginal people can be negotiated quickly and to the benefit of all.
The Jawoyn Association negotiated the Mount Todd mine agreement after the High Court's Mabo decision, with the mining company, and the Territory and Federal Governments.
The Jawoyn people have gone on to negotiate a contract mining joint venture, successful training and employment programs, and exploration agreements.
Today, the association launches its five-year development plan.
Grant Watt from the Minerals Council says the Jawoyn people are rightfully proud of their achievements.
Mr Watt says the plan looks excellent, and he wishes the association every bit of success over its lifetime.
AURORA AUSTRALIS HEADING SOUTH AGAIN
It's hoped more Antarctic secrets will be revealed during the next voyage of the research and supply ship, the Aurora Australis.
The vessel leaves Hobart this afternoon on a two-month voyage to investigate the continent's ancient sea beds.
Scientists aboard the vessel plan to gather sea bed data to help determine the evolution of Antarctica and its ice sheets over the past few million years.
They're to conduct an off-shore geological drill in the Casey region south of Perth, and scout for another site 1,400 km west along the continent's coast.
A study of Antarctic and Southern Ocean volcanoes are also on the trip's agenda, including Australia's only active volcano, Big Ben.
Satellite photos have revealed it's erupted within the past month.
CONTROL OF TASSIE GOLD MINE UP FOR GRABS
The battle for control of what promises to be Tasmania's biggest gold mine is expected to hot up this week.
The Sydney-based company, Otter Gold, is in the box seat to take effective control of Allstate Explorations, which manages the project to redevelop the old Tasmania Mine at Beaconsfield.

Otter has obtained a waiver of takeover rules from the Australian Securities Commission to lift its interest in Allstate from 47 to just over 49 percent and continued to buy shares in the company last week.

Tasmanian-based Beaconsfield Gold, Allstate's joint venture partner, mounted an unsuccessful takeover bid for the company last year, and is appealing to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal for an injuction against the ASC decision.
However, the appeal will not be heard until Friday, giving Otter valuable time to acquire more shares and gain control of Allstate and the Beaconsfield gold project.
MORE CASH FOR QLD DRUG PROBE
The Queensland Government has agreed to give more money to the Criminal Justice Commission's inquiry into police involvement in the drug trade.
State Cabinet has approved an extra A$1.5 million dollars following a request by inquiry head Bill Carter QC.
Mr Carter said he needed more money to do his job properly.
Premier, Rob Borbidge, said last week that he wanted to see what the investigation unveiled before committing extra funds.
Attorney-General, Denver Beanland, says the decision was made following a meeting yesterday with Mr Carter and CJC Chairman, Frank Clair.
Mr Beanland says the Government is determined to ensure that the state's police force is free of corruption.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
